newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to complain about trade obstacles with U.S..
newsitem.headline: Israel to complain about trade obstacles with U.S..

text.p: Israel said on Wednesday it would raise the matter of U.S. practices it says hamper bilateral free trade when the two countries meet next week to review their free trade area (FTA) agreement.
The Industry and Trade Ministry said Washington's "unilateral interpretation" of the agreement's rules of origin "present an obstacle to trade between Israel and the United States".
"As a result of these unilateral interpretations, Israeli companies have customs problems in the United States that have prevented the free and secure flow of trade," the ministry said.

Israeli officials will also seek to eliminate customs and other barriers on Israeli products moving between the three countries belonging to the North America Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), the ministry said.
Israel has separate free trade agreements with each of the NAFTA countries -- the United States, Canada and Mexico.
Other U.S. decisions had made it difficult for Israel to compete in certain government tenders, the ministry said.

The joint committee overseeing the FTA between Israel and the United States, which was signed in 1985, will be meeting in Washington. The ministry said the meeting was scheduled after the U.S. complained about Israel's import policies.

"While many of their complaints were exaggerated and claims of Israeli violations of the agreement unjustified, we will make every effort to move closer to the American position and solve the problems," the ministry said.
